description: A slew limiter with separate rise and fall times that becomes a looping envelope when the mode switch is moved, after Black Noise Modular's Slew/LFO

params.text: Bends the rise and fall shapes: fully clockwise each segment is a straight line, and turning it back rounds them into an exponential curve
Sets how long the output takes to climb, slowest fully clockwise; with the rate switch slow and no capacitor chosen that runs from 8ms to reach 10V up to 8 seconds
Sets how long the output takes to fall, slowest fully clockwise; with the rate switch slow and no capacitor chosen that runs from 8ms to fall 10V up to 8 seconds
Switches between LFO, where the output cycles between 0V and 10V on its own, and Slew, where the output chases the voltage at the input jack
Switches between the slow range and the fast range; fast shortens every time by a factor of forty, reaching 200 microseconds for 10V and running the LFO up to audio rates
Stands in for a capacitor added to the hardware: none, about 10 microfarads for times of 1.2 seconds to 20 minutes, or about 100 microfarads for 2 minutes to 33 hours

inputs.text: Adds to the RISE knob, and a negative voltage here shortens the rise; the jack reads from -5V to 10V and anything outside that is clamped
Adds to the FALL knob, and a negative voltage here shortens the fall; the jack reads from -5V to 10V and anything outside that is clamped
The voltage the output chases while the mode switch is set to Slew; in LFO mode nothing patched here is read

outputs.text: The slewed or cycling voltage, 0V to 10V, except in LFO mode with the rate switch fast, where it is shifted down to -5V to 5V unless the centring menu item is switched off

notes: in LFO mode the input jack is ignored and the output runs on its own; in Slew mode the output stays where it is until a voltage arrives at the input
the number of polyphonic channels is taken from whichever of the three inputs carries most, and the output carries that many
menu: Oversampling (fast mode only): Off, x2, x4, x8, x16 — runs the shape at this multiple of the sample rate and filters the result back down, and it is applied only while the rate switch is fast
Centre waveform at audio rates — moves the LFO output down to -5V to 5V while the rate switch is fast, so an audio-rate waveform carries no direct voltage; switching it off leaves 0V to 10V

inputs.0:
-5 to 10V · continuous · polyphonic

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.1:
-5 to 10V · continuous · polyphonic

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
